entries.title: How the Cubs' James Triantos is blocking out the impending trade deadline
entries.summary: <p>The Aug. 3 trade deadline is hours away. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> badly need <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/30/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-pitching-starting-rotation-matthew-boyd-shota-imanaga-colin-rea-david-peterson-javier-assad-tarik-skubal" >starting pitchers and could use help in the bullpen</a>. Whenever a potential trade candidate is scratched from a start, the news spreads on social media and ignites speculation about impending moves.</p><p>It’s hard for anybody who’s invested in baseball not to pay attention and think about which big names will be in new places by Monday night. Yet rookie infielder James Triantos, a potential trade chip who could be directly impacted if the Cubs do something, isn’t using brain space on the subject.</p><p>“It’s not worth it to me to stress out over stuff that I can’t control like that,” Triantos told the Sun-Times before the Cubs’ game Saturday against the Yankees. “So, I just focus on showing up at the field and being ready to go every single day. This is a great opportunity to have, and I just want to take advantage of it.”</p><p>Sparingly used since getting recalled July 24 from Triple-A Iowa, Triantos made his first big-league start Saturday, batting ninth and serving as the Cubs’ designated hitter against New York lefty Max Fried. Before Saturday, Triantos had just two at-bats.</p><p>That didn’t seem to sour him on the value of his first look at major-league life with the Cubs.</p><p>Triantos is eager to soak up whatever information he can during his first stay in the big leagues. He said the experience has been “amazing,” taking bits of info from his new teammates with shiny resumes and track records of producing at the highest level. He’s observing how consistent the veterans are with their routines and preparing, both mentally and physically.</p><p>“It’s everything I can dream of,” Triantos said. “It’s such a great opportunity to learn and be around the guys. It’s fun to win.”</p><p>For additional pointers on maximizing this time, Triantos said he’s spoken a lot with former Cubs prospect Owen Caissie, one of his best friends. Caissie was called up Aug. 14 last year.</p><p>“He learned a lot from these guys,” Triantos said. “Just asking him the ins and outs and what I should be ready for and everything like that.”</p><p>That connection might turn out to be ironic or fitting, depending on the point of view.</p><p>Caissie didn’t have long to apply what he learned for the Cubs. He played in 12 games and had 26 at-bats but that was the sum of his Cubs tenure, which ended when he was traded to the Marlins as part of the Edward Cabrera deal.</p><p>A second-round pick in 2021, Triantos has steadily climbed through the Cubs system. A right-handed hitter with good contact skills, Triantos has attributes that could be attractive to a suitor looking for prospects that should be ready to contribute in the major leagues now or soon.</p><p>And there’s also the matter of where Triantos could play for the Cubs. In six minor-league seasons he has 38 home runs, so he doesn’t profile as a hitter who would fully transition to a corner outfield spot. He is further blocked by Nico Hoerner, Dansby Swanson and Alex Bregman, who will be at second base, shortstop and third base, respectively, for the foreseeable future.</p><p>None of these permutations are bothering Triantos. He doesn’t have X/Twitter on his phone and doesn’t look for information or chatter with his name in it.</p><p>“I get paid to live out my dream. It’s not that hard,” Triantos said of ignoring the noise. “This is what I love to do. This is my job. This is my favorite thing to do. It’s all I’ve loved to do forever.”</p>

entries.title: Robert Lewandowski scores twice in victorious home debut with Fire
entries.summary: <p>Robert Lewandowski scored two goals, including the winner, in his home debut for the Fire, helping them beat Charlotte 2-1 on Saturday at Soldier Field.</p><p>Lewandowski, who made the move from FC Barcelona in a two-year deal with Chicago, equalized in the 20th minute off a screamer from outside the box that tied the game at 1.</p><p>He connected on his second goal of the night in the 68th minute with a go-ahead shot to the bottom left corner to seal the win for the Fire (9-6-2), who played their first home match in over two months.</p><p>Pep Biel gave Charlotte (7-7-4) an early lead with a shot from the right side of the box on an assist from Idan Toklomati.</p><p>Charlotte pushed for an equalizer late and earned a corner in stoppage time, but Chicago held on to preserve the one-goal lead.</p><p>Charlotte entered the match unbeaten in its last two games, but dropped its third straight against the Fire.</p><h3><b>Up next</b></h3><p>Charlotte: Takes on Pumas UNAM in Leagues Cup group stage play on Tuesday.</p><p>Chicago: Visit Club Necaxa in Leagues Cup group stage play on Thursday.<br></p>

entries.title: Woman shot in Austin carjacking
entries.summary: <p>A 36-year-old woman was shot during a carjacking early Saturday in Austin, Chicago police said.</p><p>Officers responded to a call of a person shot at about 12:37 a.m. along the 4600 block of West Fifth Avenue, police said.</p><p>The woman was getting out of her car when a man approached, fired shots and demanded access to her vehicle before fleeing, according to police.</p><p>The woman suffered a gunshot wound to the back and was treated at the scene by the Chicago Fire Department personnel, police said. She was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in good condition.</p><p>Area Four Detectives were investigating.</p>

entries.title: Federal judge tosses Trump administration lawsuit seeking full access to Illinois voter rolls
entries.summary: <p>A downstate federal judge has rejected an effort by President Donald Trump’s administration to obtain full access to Illinois’ voter registration database, including sensitive personal data on more than 8 million residents statewide.</p><p>The Justice Department’s request for the voter rolls “to ascertain Illinois’s compliance” with federal law isn’t a legitimate reason for demanding the vast trove of data, “as it does not relate to any suspected violation of voting,” Judge Colleen Lawless wrote in a 14-page opinion issued Friday.</p><p>The decision from Illinois’ Central District court in Springfield marked the 19th ruling nationwide against lawsuits filed by the Trump DOJ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2025/12/19/illinois-voter-rolls-voting-lawsuit-president-trump" target="_blank" ><u>over the past year</u></a> in what it has called an effort to ensure election integrity.</p><p>Trump has long falsely claimed rampant voter fraud led to his 2020 election loss to former President Joe Biden, though cases of fraud have proven <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/democracy/2024/05/15/election-disinformation-democracy-solutions-project" target="_blank" ><u>exceedingly rare anywhere in the country</u></a>.</p><p>“If the Attorney General could simply justify his demand with a statement of any purpose whatsoever, the requirement that he specify his purpose (and his basis) would be pointless and it would provide him with unfettered authority to demand voting records,” Lawless wrote.</p><p>Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul said the ruling underscores the fact “voters can remain confident that our elections are fair and secure.”</p><p>“The Trump administration’s demand for Illinois’ unredacted voter registration list is part of the president’s ongoing efforts to undermine and sow doubt in U.S. elections,” Raoul said in a statement. “But in Illinois, we are focused on ensuring voters’ access to the ballot box while protecting their personal information.</p><p>“The Constitution is clear: States have authority to administer and regulate elections,” Raoul continued. “Courts have consistently ruled that the Department of Justice’s attempts to commandeer unredacted voter registration lists are unlawful.”</p><p>DOJ officials couldn’t immediately be reached for comment.</p><p>The Trump administration requested Illinois’ full voter database last July, and the Illinois State Board of Elections provided voters’ names, addresses and ages at registration — but not dates of birth, ID numbers or social security numbers, as limited by state law.</p><p>That prompted the DOJ to sue “to protect American citizens from vote dilution,” but local election authorities are responsible for most of that information, and handing it over would violate federal privacy law, too, Illinois officials argued.</p><p>The American Civil Liberties Union of Illinois hailed the decision, and Ami Gandhi, director of the Midwest Voting Rights Program with Chicago Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights, called it “a critical victory for the privacy rights of every Illinois voter.”</p><p>“The federal government's attempt to seize sensitive personal records was an unprecedented overreach designed to intimidate voters and fuel false narratives about our election systems,” Gandhi said in a statement. “By rejecting this demand, the court has sent a clear message that our democratic process will not be weaponized to harass or suppress Illinois voters, particularly naturalized citizens and people returning home from incarceration who are disproportionately targeted by these efforts.”</p>

entries.title: David Peterson strong again in Cubs' 5-2 win over Yankees
entries.summary: <p>When pitcher<b> David Peterson </b>joined the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> after a June 25 trade with the Mets, the move wasn’t expected to change the path of the pennant race or give his new team an ace. <b>Edward Cabrera </b>and <b>Ben Brown </b>had just landed on the injured list, joining <b>Justin Steele</b>, <b>Cade Horton </b>and <b>Jameson Taillon</b>, meaning the Cubs just wanted somebody who was healthy.</p><p>Peterson, who had a 6.09 ERA in 68 innings with the Mets, qualified. He <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/26/cubs-david-peterson-trade-mets-starting-rotation-craig-counsell-all-star-pitcher" >was available</a>, not terribly expensive to get and experienced.</p><p>“We were wondering who was going to start a game for us,” manager <b>Craig Counsell </b>said. “That’s where we were at.”</p><p>Peterson has done more than just stabilize the rotation and eat innings. He’s been a key part of the staff, which he showed again in the Cubs’ 5-2 win Saturday over the Yankees.</p><p>Peterson went 6 1/3 innings, giving up two runs (one earned) while matching a season high with eight strikeouts. He has a 1.52 ERA in his last four outings, and has completed at least five innings while allowing two or fewer runs in five of his six Cubs starts.</p><p>As for what Peterson’s changed since joining the Cubs, he said there’s “nothing huge or new.” Instead, it was restoring old patterns and using his lower body more efficiently to take stress off his arm, which allows better command and pitch shapes.</p><p>“That’s kind of the biggest thing, and then just kind of tweaking things as we go and finding spots we can get better,” Peterson said.</p><h2><b>In the clutch</b></h2><p>Despite Peterson’s work, the Cubs trailed 2-1 in the bottom of the seventh. <b>Nico Hoerner </b>changed that with a leadoff solo home run that survived the brisk wind blowing in.</p><p>With two outs, <b>Pedro Ramirez </b>pinch-hit for <b>James Triantos </b>and worked a walk, keeping the inning alive for <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b>. Facing lefty <b>Brent Headrick</b>, Crow-Armstrong pulled a slider into the right field corner for a triple that brought in Ramirez and put the Cubs ahead.</p><p>“I know it’s spring training, but [Ramirez] definitely made a big impression in spring, just with how he carried himself,” Hoerner said. “He’s humble but confident and enjoys the game, has a good sense of humor. He’s going to have a really great career, so he’s been huge for us.”</p><p><b>Seiya Suzuki </b>completed the Cubs’ seventh-inning rally with another run-scoring single, though he was called out when he over-slid second and was tagged.</p><p>“That was a stretch of some really good at-bats that inning,” Counsell said.</p><h2><b>Cabrera’s rehab</b></h2><p>Cabrera<b> </b>(left hamstring strain) made the first start of his rehab assignment Friday for Triple-A Iowa. Cabrera pitched 1 2/3 innings and gave up three runs, but more importantly than his numbers, Cabrera came through the outing healthy, throwing 43 pitches and topping out at 98.8 mph.</p><p>“We’ll move to the next step [and] increase the pitches,” Counsell said. “He kind of showed he hadn’t been out there for a month, but that’s expected and normal. Just keep building from here.”</p><p>Cabrera’s next start for Iowa will be Wednesday, and he is expected to need another after that before rejoining the Cubs.</p>

entries.title: First pitch arrives in Springfield for Women's Pro Baseball League: 'We're ballplayers, too'
entries.summary: <p>SPRINGFIELD — The Jimmy Dugan character portrayed by Tom Hanks might have told his Rockford Peaches women's baseball team in the 1992 classic “A League of Their Own” that there’s “no crying in baseball.”</p><p>But there were tears of joy shed at the inaugural Women’s Pro Baseball League game Saturday in Springfield, where real-life Rockford Peach Maybelle Blair, 99, threw her ceremonial first pitch from a wheelchair to kick off <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/2026/07/31/womens-pro-baseball-comes-home-to-illinois-paving-the-way-for-next-generation-of-ballplayers" >the sold-out season opener</a>.</p><p>More than 4,000 poncho-wearing fans packed the rain-soaked stands, singing along to Shania Twain’s “Man! I Feel Like a Woman!” as the Los Angeles Queens went to bat against the New York Heights after a 90-minute weather delay.</p><p>Both teams came stacked with star power. Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato and former Little League champion and outfielder Mo’Ne Davis represented LA, while Team USA’s powerhouse duo of outfielder Kylee Lahners and catcher Denae Benites anchored the Heights.</p><p>Nine-year-old Lena Shackleford of Virginia attended the historic game two years after participating in a catching lesson with Benites in Washington D.C.</p><p>Decked out in royal-blue Heights gear, Shackleford said she dreams to be a catcher like Benites, who hit the first, and so far only, home run of the season.</p><p>“There's only like two times I've been in a tournament that's all girls, so I'm kind of used to being the only one.” Shackleford said. “It feels really great to know that there are other [girls] out there.”</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: White Sox acquiring Mariners starter Luis Castillo for reliever Seranthony Dominguez, two prospects
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The White Sox are going for it. To what degree, we’ll see.</p><p>They made their first splash before the trade deadline at 5 p.m. Monday by acquiring Mariners right-hander Luis Castillo late Saturday for reliever Seranthony Dominguez and prospects Nolan Jones and Boston Smith. The Sox also are picking up the rest of Castillo’s contract.</p><p>Castillo, 33, is a three-time All-Star who can add length and playoff experience to a rotation in need of both. Outside of Sean Burke, Sox starters generally are done by the fifth inning, and none has pitched in the postseason. But Castillo’s 5.06 ERA in 20 games this season (17 starts) is the worst of his career.</p><p>He figures to get more run support with the Sox, who rank ninth in the majors with 522 runs. The Mariners are 28th with 447. Castillo received three runs or fewer of support in 15 starts and allowed four runs or fewer 13 times.</p><p>Castillo might take rookie left-hander Noah Schultz’s spot in the rotation. After two stinkers coming out of the All-Star break, Schultz delivered five innings of one-run ball Saturday against the Rays. But that one run was one too many in a 1-0 loss. Schultz followed opener Jordan Hicks, who threw a perfect first.</p><p>After rumblings that the Sox were unlikely to make such a move, general manager Chris Getz dealt a quality prospect in Smith, a catcher who ranks 15th overall in the Sox’ system, according to MLB.com.</p><p>Catcher isn’t a strength in the organization. Kyle Teel has missed much of the season with injuries, and Edgar Quero and Drew Romo aren’t providing enough offense. At three minor-league levels this season, Smith has a 1.037 OPS with 22<br>home runs.</p><p>Jones, an outfielder acquired from the Guardians in June, also has some pop, though he isn’t ranked among the Sox’ top 30 prospects. In Triple-A with both franchises this season, Jones has an .807 OPS with 14 homers.</p><p>Dominguez, whom the Sox signed to a two-year, $20 million contract in the offseason, lost his closer job about a month ago but has started to come on. He had one of his best innings of the season Saturday, striking out two and throwing 11 of 14 pitches for strikes in a perfect seventh against the Rays. </p><div class="PageListL" data-module entries.title: Review: Geese soars above the haters as the controversial New York rockers debunk the myths haunting the band
entries.summary: <p>In the year since the release of its latest album “Getting Killed,” Geese has been in the crosshairs of many a music critic and music snob.</p><p>The New York rockers have been accused of being industry plants, scene interlopers and marketing manipulators at best. Their “Saturday Night Live” debut was picked apart. Their family lines were investigated for possible record label moles. A band nowadays apparently can’t actually be good and have a sudden rise before being prematurely autopsied.</p><p>But at Lollapalooza Saturday, Geese spread its wings and properly debunked the myths that keep haunting the band. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-170000" The quality of the show is ‘up in the air,’ so to speak.”</p><p>To the aforementioned music snob, it probably is ammo in the band’s argument. For the casual fan, no one seemed to know any difference. A sizable crowd flocked over to the Allianz stage to catch the controversial act, though it was unclear if that all was truly for Geese or hangers on for Olivia Dean who headlined on the adjoining T-Mobile stage right after.</p><p>“Who’s on after us?” asked Winter. Some responded correctly. “Nobody!” and “Who cares?” said others. In either case, it was a win for the quartet who are just weird and mysterious enough to turn heads.</p><p>The music rose to the occasion, with Winter’s inner Lou Reed and Julian Casablancas shining on songs like on “2112,” “100 Horses” and “Cowboy Nudes,” matched by the on-point playing of fellow guitarist Emily Green, bassist Dominic DiGesu and drummer Max Bassin. They all operated with great cohesion and rule-breaking gumption, no more so than in the brutal blues rocker “Trinidad” that could be their best work.</p><p>When <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2025/12/17/review-cameron-winter-rockefeller-chapel-chicago-show-heavy-metal" >Winter headlined the Rockefeller Chapel</a> at the University of Chicago last December under the guise of his solo album “Heavy Metal,” he proved his gifts, just himself and a piano. But on the Lolla stage with the full band, it’s tenfold. His charisma as a front man is undefinable. It may not be in line with the fervent fans who hail him as this generation’s Kurt Cobain. Then again, Courtney Love is a very vocal supporter of him and the band so there’s that.</p><p>Formed in 2016, Geese comes from the holy grail of Brooklyn, an untouchable lineage to some, but the quartet wears the Television, Velvet Underground and Strokes influences well on songs like fan favorites “Taxes,” “Bow Down” and “Cobra” without coming off as pantomime. Throw in a little Leonard Cohen on slow peak songs “Au Pays du Cocaine” and “I See Myself.” Maybe some Henry Rollins on bar brawler “Jesse.” Who could hate any of that? entries.title: Harvey police identify 2 victims in fatal shooting
entries.summary: <p>Authorities have identified two people found fatally shot inside a far south suburban home Thursday.</p><p>The victims were identified as Jwon L. Martin, a 46-year-old Harvey woman, and Aaron Jones, a 50-year-old Harvey man, according to a spokesperson for the Harvey Police Department. </p><p>Police were called to a home near 150th Street and Vine Avenue, where officers found the two victims with gunshot wounds, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-suburbs/2026/07/30/harvey-dog-shooting-150th-vine" target="_blank" >Harvey police said Thursday</a>.</p><p>Both victims were pronounced dead at the scene, police said.</p><p>Two dogs had also been shot. Authorities said one dog died and the other was in critical condition as of Thursday.</p><p>The department said the investigation was active and ongoing.</p><p>Anyone with information is asked to contact the Harvey Police Department Detective Division at 708-331-3030 ext. 226.</p>

entries.title: Heavy rain disrupts commutes, Lollapalooza as more flooding hits Chicago area
entries.summary: <p>Chicagoans might get a break from the rain Sunday after the latest round of soggy weather disrupted traffic, flooded more homes and upended the schedule at Day 3 of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/01/heavy-rains-delay-opening-of-doors-at-lollapalooza-on-day-3" >Lollapalooza</a>.</p><p>Forecasters expected drier conditions arrive into Sunday with highs in the mid-70s, according to the National Weather Service.</p><p>NWS meteorologist David King said Saturday's highest rainfall totals in the area fell in eastern Kendall County, where up to 4 inches of rain fell, while parts of far northeastern Will County and eastern DuPage County from Downers Grove to Elmhurst were soaked with 2 to 3 inches.</p><p>"A constant stream of intermittent showers" prompted flash flood warnings across the area, King said.</p><p>"It's been a good soaking rain for much of the area," he said. "If you're traveling, be a little more cautious and allow more room between you and the vehicle ahead."</p><p>Chicago's Office of Emergency Management and Communications was coordinating with city departments and other agencies in response to the storms, according to spokesperson Mary May.</p><p>Officials were still assessing the impact of the rainfall that came on the heels of several other storms this summer that have caused headaches for thousands of residents with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/07/27/weather-storms-heat-wind" >flooding and seepage</a>. Four <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/07/28/storms-flooding-tornadoes-damage-worker-missing-power-outage" >tornadoes</a> were confirmed in the weather system that raked the area last week. </p><p>Flooded roads posed hazards Saturday, as Illinois State Police responded at about 7:45 a.m. to southbound Interstate 55 at Joliet Road, with a report of water across all lanes, Sgt. Jason Wilson said. </p><p>There weren't major roadway closures, crashes or stranded vehicles linked to flooding as of Saturday evening, but images posted to social media showed part of a retaining wall appeared to have collapsed at the Lawrence Avenue exit on the Kennedy Expressway.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/ChicagoScanner?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#ChicagoScanner</a> <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Chicago?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Chicago</a> <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/ChiTraffic?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#ChiTraffic</a> <br><br>Inbound Kennedy Expy I-90 at the Lawrence exit the outer retaining wall to the exit ramp has collapsed onto the right embankment of the inbound lanes<br><br>Ramp currently closed for inspection, no current lane closures on the Kennedy but that… <a href="https://t.co/Wy3qmDdRbw">pic.twitter.com/Wy3qmDdRbw</a></p>— WindyCity Weather and News (@WindyCityWxMan) <a href="https://x.com/WindyCityWxMan/status/2083595405367882071?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 1, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>In Clarendon Hills, about 3 inches of rain fell over a two-hour period, resulting in flooded and impassable roadways, flooded yards and several reports of flooded basements, Village Manager Paul Dalen said. The village's Public Works and Police departments closed flooded roadways with traffic cones and cleared blocked storm drains to help alleviate flooding and restore safe conditions.</p><p>Village The city also urged drivers to avoid passing through standing water on streets, viaducts and other low-lying areas.</p><p>State police encouraged motorists to slow down, increase following distances and avoid using cruise control if they encounter water on the roadway.</p><p>Wilson reiterated the importance of avoiding driving through floodwater and said residents should call 911 to report floodwater emergencies.</p><p>Chicago residents can report flooded basements, standing water on streets or viaduct flooding by visiting 311.chicago.gov, using the CHI311 app or calling 311. OEMC encourages residents to stay informed by enabling weather alerts on their mobile phones and monitoring local media, weather apps or weather radios for updates.</p>
